subject: axolotl
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: axolotl with frilly pink gills.
Style: chibi.
reasoning:
I'm planning a chibi axolotl design with a big head, short body, finned tail, stubby legs with toes, feathery gills, a wide smile, and large shiny eyes, scaling the proportions down from a real axolotl's size into a cute stylized form.

Now I'm working out the skeleton: a root hips joint with spine chains leading up to a neck and head, plus a separate tail chain extending backward with several joints for smooth curvature, keeping parent-child relationships simple throughout.

For the body geometry, I'm planning separate sweeps for the torso and tail rather than one combined path—overlapping spheres at the hips joint will hide the seam between them. The torso sweep uses elliptical cross-sections sized to keep the belly just above the floor, and the head is a scaled sphere flattened to look wide and low.

I'm working out skin tones next: a countershade pink base with lighter belly and darker back, plus subtle dark freckle spots layered on top. Then I'm positioning a lower jaw piece as a separate flattened half-sphere, anchored near the head joint and angled slightly forward.

Now I'm adding a mouth decal—a dark smile curve projected onto the head's front surface near the muzzle. For the eyes, I decide against an overly anime-style decal and plan small simple dark circles instead, fitting a chibi axolotl look.

I'm reconsidering decal placement using angular coordinates on the head, but switch to simpler, more reliable geometry: solid dark glossy spheres plus tiny highlight spheres for eyes. I'm working out absolute positions for the eyes relative to the head's ellipsoid center and radii, checking that candidate coordinates fall properly on the ellipsoid surface.

I'm adding flattened pink blush discs on the cheeks, positioning them on the head's surface curve and orienting them outward using a scale and direction trick, then starting to place tiny nostril dots.

Now I'm designing the gills: three stalks per side rooted near the back of the head, swept outward with a tapered bezier curve in red-pink, and adding fanned filament spikes along each stalk...

Still writing filament loops...

I'm giving each gill stalk a bone head so it's rigid, with spikes inheriting the sweep's bone automatically. I'm also considering adding hinge joints per stalk for rigging, named by side and index under the head.

Now I'm working out the actual stalk geometry: for each side and index 0-2, I'm picking base positions and fan-out directions so the three stalks spread upward, outward, and slightly back, with the lower stalk angled more outward-down.

Setting stalk length around 0.095-0.1 for a chibi-proportioned big frilly gill relative to the head width, with curved control points biased upward for a natural splay.

Now moving to the legs — I'm setting up short two-joint chains for the front legs, placing shoulder and elbow points slightly outward and down from the body to keep the stubby chibi proportions.

Still defining toe and leg geometry...

Defining the body sweep radii...

I'll keep the body mostly straight with just a slight x-curve for symmetry, then work out the dorsal fin as an extruded sail shape running from body to tail tip, defining its outline in z-y coordinates for a side profile.

Mapping out the fin outline coordinates...

For the fin color I'll use a gradient paint blending a lighter pink to a deeper rose along the vertical axis, skipping ray-line textures for simplicity. I'm considering whether to add a dorsal ridge crest, and thinking about using decal-based eye highlights instead of sphere geometry to help hit the target texture count.

Actually for the gill frills, cards along each stalk would read better and be simpler than spikes — placing small leaning cards at points swept along the stalk, with their flow following the stalk's tangent direction toward the tip.

For the texture, I'll draw a frond with fine pink strands and lighter tips, letting the card's own texture carry the coloring rather than relying on tints. I'll add a small cluster of three cards at each stalk tip for extra detail.

For the skin, I'm adding freckle-like spots, a pale belly, and a leucistic pink axolotl look with darker pink spots and dark red gills, plus a smiling mouth texture, highlighted eye pupils, and a soft radial-gradient blush decal on the cheeks.

For the eyes, I'm deciding between flat decals or textured spheres -- going with dark glossy spheres plus tiny white highlight spheres for a bulging chibi look, while keeping blush, smile, and the two-toned frond textures as the main decal set.

I'm now positioning the smile decal on the head using placement, direction, and size parameters, with a curved mouth path drawn in a wide rounded style and small corner ticks for character.

For the jaw, I'm considering whether a separate ellipsoid would sit mostly hidden inside the head, so instead I'm thinking about shaping the skull as a partial sphere geometry with an open cap at the bottom, calculating the theta angle needed to crop it cleanly below the equator.

I'm checking the geometry overlap between the jaw and skull so the smile decal stays visible — shrinking the jaw's radius and shifting its center slightly so it doesn't cover the mouth area, with the jaw's bottom edge landing around y=.006.

Now I'm confirming the head's proportions are chibi-scaled relative to the body width, then moving on to defining the skin paint pattern with pink dots for countershading.

Setting color palette and spine joint positions...

I'm worried the rear cap on the body will create an unnatural bulge where the tail meets it, so I want to blend the two into one continuous taper instead—starting the tail's radius close to the body's and shrinking it smoothly rather than abruptly.

Still tuning tail radius math...

Now I'm checking vertical clearances—making sure the body, tail, and limbs all stay above the floor line with appropriate radii, then moving on to sketch out the toe bones after the limb sweeps are set.

Writing toe capsule code...

Now I'm thinking through the hand pose, facial details like blush and nostrils, and setting up gill joints on each side of the head with named bones. I'm sketching a bezier path for the gill stalks and sweeping a capsule shape along it with a slight radius taper into the head.

Still writing card frames...

For the frond texture, I'm sketching a central stem with five pairs of thin curved branches radiating outward, plus a small tip circle, all sized to fit a 40x64 viewBox.

I'm scaling stroke widths and colors for the different face textures—a smile curve with small end ticks in ink color, and a blush texture using a pink ellipse with darker stripe accents.

For placement, I'm figuring out the cheek decal position by hitting the skull surface near the front-left with a slight downward elevation, and computing eye positions using azimuth and elevation angles derived from their x/z coordinates so they sit naturally on the upper face.

Working out exact eye socket coordinates and sphere scaling, then placing small highlight dots offset from each eye center for a glossy look.

I need to pull in the right exports from the builder module and use the rng for card variation. For the fin, I'm working out the extrusion direction so the outline's x-axis maps to world z, then checking the outline point order to avoid self-crossing edges.

Still refining fin outline coordinates...

Writing leg chain code...

Computing the gill direction vectors and tip/control points, then checking that the gill bases sit correctly within the skull's radius so they don't poke outside the head geometry.
